title: Residual-compensated mixed-precision KV cache for streaming latency-sensitive workloads
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: evaluate a residual-compensation approach for mixed-precision KV caches that pairs aggressive primary quantization (INT4/INT8/FP8) with a compact low-overhead residual correction table to reduce output quality regressions for streaming, low-latency workloads. The experiment explores trade-offs between peak GPU memory reduction, median/95th latency impact under continuous batching, and model quality (token-level divergence, downstream perplexity on production prompt sets). We target workloads where prefix caching is large (long conversation context) and latency SLOs are tight (<= 8ms P50 additional cost).

Scope: prototype runtime encoder/decoder support for storing primary KV blocks in INT4/INT8/FP8 plus an auxiliary residual vector per block encoded in INT8. Residuals are optionally applied during dequantization for tokens flagged as high-sensitivity (classification from a small heuristic model). Evaluate strategies for: static per-layer quant config, per-block dynamic residual activation, and on-request fallback to FP16 for worst-case divergence. Measure end-to-end in hosted and dedicated-like configs (single-GPU A100 and multi-GPU sharded setups).
acceptance_criteria: Prototype runtime can persist and load mixed-precision KV pages (primary quant + residual table) without model-format changes
Achieve >= 45% GPU KV memory reduction vs FP16 baseline while keeping downstream perplexity delta <= 1.0% on PROD prompt set
Median added tail latency (P50/P95) from residual application under continuous batching <= 2ms (P50) and <= 6ms (P95)
Automated regression test that flags cases where token-level divergence > 2 tokens for more than 0.5% of requests
Benchmarks and a clear rollout plan documented for canary, with fallback policy to FP16 that triggers based on live divergence signals
progress_updates: 2025-02-15 - Kickoff: design reviewed with Runtime Leads and Research. Decision to prototype residuals as INT8 delta from primary quantized values to keep decode cheap.

2025-02-20 - Data sampling: collected KV statistics from 200M tokens of production traces to build per-layer sensitivity maps. Observed attention heads in early layers are less sensitive to INT4 but later layers spike error.
2025-02-26 - Implementation: added encode/decode hooks in runtime with a compact metadata page format. Initial microbenchmarks show encode overhead ~0.7ms per KV block on A100.

2025-03-01 - Benchmarks: INT4+residual prototype reduces KV footprint by ~52% vs FP16 for 32k-context models; downstream eval on curated prompts shows perplexity increase 0.8% vs FP16 (within target). Latency: median +1.9ms when residuals applied; P95 +5.4ms under continuous batching of 16 requests.

2025-03-03 - Trade-off decision: enable heuristic that only applies residuals for request tokens with high-sensitivity score > 0.6 (from offline head-sensitivity model). This reduces residual application frequency to ~22% of tokens and cuts median latency overhead to +0.6ms while preserving 0.9% PPL delta.
2025-03-05 - Next: run multi-GPU sharded experiments and integrate fallback signal into the tracing pipeline. Prepare PR and canary rollout doc.
